title: Approximation Strategy for Timed Tests
tagline: Year 4 — Deciding in seconds whether to estimate or calculate, and choosing the precision from the option spacing

introduction.overview: Approximation is a strategic decision as much as an arithmetic skill. For every question you must decide in a few seconds whether an estimate will separate the options, how precise it must be, and whether to fall back to exact calculation. The decision rule is simple: compute the gap between the nearest options as a percentage; if your estimate's possible error is smaller than half that gap, estimate; otherwise calculate.
introduction.placementRelevance: Timed tests reward candidates who estimate when they can and calculate only when they must.
introduction.realWorldContext: Estimating before committing resources is standard practice in planning.

learningObjectives: Compute the relative gap between options
Estimate the error of a rounding
Choose the rounding that keeps error small
Fall back to exact calculation when needed

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: Relative error = |estimate − exact| ÷ exact. Relative gap = difference between options ÷ the smaller option.

coreDefinitions: Relative gap: the size of the difference between two options in percent.
Half-gap rule: estimate only if the error is less than half the gap.
Rounding error: difference caused by rounding.
Precision: how close an estimate must be.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: The question is not how accurate you can be, but how accurate you must be.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Look at the options first. Find the smallest gap. Choose a rounding whose error is clearly smaller than half of it.

mainNarrative: Options 420 and 450 differ by 30, a gap of 7.1%. The half-gap is 3.6%: an estimate with error under 2% is enough.
Rounding 4,180 to 4,200 gives an error of 20 ÷ 4,180 = 0.48%.
For a product, the relative errors of the factors add: rounding 52 to 50 (3.8%) and 4,180 to 4,200 (0.5%) gives about 4.3%.
If the options are 24%, 25%, 26%, the gap is 4%; half is 2%; rough rounding (error over 4%) is not enough, so calculate.
When estimate and options disagree by a large margin, recheck: you may have mis-set the problem.

deepDiveAspects.title: Round in opposite directions
deepDiveAspects.content: In a product, rounding one up and one down partially cancels.

traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Find the smallest option gap, halve it, and estimate if your error is smaller than that.

commonMistakes.mistake: Rounding both up in a quotient

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: Eliminate options far from the estimate.
placementTips.questionSelectionAdvice: Always look at the options first.
placementTips.recruiterInsight: The skill is deciding, not estimating.
